reasoning:
I'm working out whether to keep rules (b) and (c) or simplify to just the remaining ≤ 30 condition, tracing through round 1's timing to see whether the fourth arrival at the far end satisfies that threshold depending on whether the first crossing time is fast or slow.

Looking at round 3 and round 4 data, remaining values like 33, 27, 37, and 21-28 line up with B/C recordings in a way that's consistent with the ≤30 cutoff, and the round-1 case likely involved a fast cube with first_cross_t under 30, which would fit the simplified rule.

Timing alone seems to explain everything, including the turnaround case the earlier refusal worried about. I'll commit to the edit that drops the frame-based velocity check and relies solely on crossings and first_cross_t, removing the directional note as the report suggests, and I'm now identifying the exact passages to swap out for this simplified version.

press takes roughly 25-30 timesteps to land), based purely on predicted arrival time rather than direction of motion. For rule B, I'm refining the condition so it applies when crossings == N-1 and remaining exceeds 30 while the cube is still running out before the predicted turnaround, even quite close to that turnaround point.

For the fallback, I'm simplifying it to just choose C immediately in the remaining cases. I'm also considering adjusting the intro description so it clearly states the press lands as the cube reaches the target for the Nth time, tying the timing language together more precisely.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: The button must be pressed one arrival early: when N-1 arrivals have happened and the cube is on its way back toward the target, so the press lands as the cube reaches the target for the Nth time.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: The button must be pressed one arrival early: when N-1 arrivals have happened and the predicted Nth arrival is at most 30 timesteps away, so the press, which takes roughly 25-30 timesteps to land, lands as the cube reaches the target for the Nth time.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: then decide using the updated crossings and first_cross_t values and the cube motion in this step's frames:
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: then decide using the updated crossings and first_cross_t values alone:

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: - Determine the cube's direction from the last two frames shown at this step, using their timesteps: v = (cube_x at the last frame - cube_x at the previous frame) / (last timestep - previous timestep). Always divide by the time gap. Take the cube's side at the last frame (smaller_x if cube_x < target_x, larger_x if cube_x > target_x). The cube is HEADING BACK toward the target if it is on the larger_x side and v < 0, or on the smaller_x side and v > 0, or its cube_x is identical in the last two frames (fully stopped at the turnaround). Otherwise it is RUNNING OUT (moving away from the target on its current side); this includes the case where the two frames lie on different sides, since the cube has just crossed. Do not treat a small |v| as the turnaround: cube speed varies by a factor of three across episodes, and a slow cube that has just crossed is still far from returning. Do not use |cube_x - target_x| shrinking or growing as the test: it shrinks across a crossing even though the cube is then moving away.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: - Do not read the cube's direction or speed from the frames to make the decision: cube speed varies threefold across episodes and changes around the turnaround, and the predicted arrival time computed from first_cross_t decides on its own.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: - Choose C 'press button to stop the cube' if crossings == N-1 AND any of: (a) remaining <= 30 timesteps (the press takes roughly 25-30 timesteps to land); (b) the timestep of the scene at this decision step is at or past the predicted turnaround (2N-2)*first_cross_t, with no slack (equivalently remaining <= first_cross_t); (c) the cube is HEADING BACK by the test above. No point is needed.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: - Choose C 'press button to stop the cube' if and only if crossings == N-1 AND remaining <= 30 timesteps (the press takes roughly 25-30 timesteps to land, so it is started once the predicted Nth arrival is at most 30 timesteps away). Whether the cube is still running out, stopped at its turnaround, or already heading back toward the target makes no difference: being past the turnaround or moving back is not enough while remaining > 30. No point is needed.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: and crossings == N-1 while the cube is RUNNING OUT by the test above with remaining > 30 and the scene timestep still before the predicted turnaround (2N-2)*first_cross_t (including the step right after the (N-1)th crossing, however slowly the cube is gliding, and while it is still on its way out to the far end, even when only a few timesteps short of the turnaround).
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: and crossings == N-1 while remaining > 30, whatever the cube is doing (the step right after the (N-1)th crossing, however slowly the cube is gliding; the cube on its way out to the far end; the cube stopped at the turnaround; and the cube already past the turnaround and heading back toward the target, as long as more than 30 timesteps remain).

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: choose C immediately if the cube is HEADING BACK by the test above or remaining <= 30, otherwise B.

revision.refused: The suggestion to replace the timing rules with a distance-over-expected-speed estimate of time-to-target stays out: the period-based prediction from first_cross_t already separates every recorded press (remaining 14-28) from every recorded wait (remaining 33 and above) across rounds 2, 3 and 4 with the single threshold remaining <= 30, while per-step speed is unreliable near the turnaround and varies threefold across episodes. No memory change is committed: crossings, first_cross_t and scene_frame were written correctly at the failed step. Removing rules (b) and (c) does not undo the round-2 concern that a fixed window would miss the turnaround press in a slow episode: this round's episode shows a cube at its turnaround with 37 timesteps remaining recorded as B, so the turnaround and heading-back clauses were the over-eager ones, and the round-1 coasting case (a fast cube, quarter period under 30) is still pressed by the timing rule. The round-1 refusal stands: C is never chosen merely because crossings reached N-1.
